facets.name: Tradition (home + secondary)
facets.question: Which body of knowledge, practice or tradition does it bring to making AI go well? First value = home (exactly one); then 0-2 traditions it also draws on substantially (3 for hubs, up to 4 for generalist funders).
facets.role_in_ui: Primary facet. The FIRST value is the home (exactly one): it sets the entry's sector among 14 equal-angle wedges in wheel order, grouped into four contiguous family arcs (Sciences & engineering: Safety, Formal, Life & systems; Minds & inner life: AI minds, Psychology, Contemplative, Religion; Humanities & cultures: Philosophy, Arts, Indigenous; Society & institutions: Law, Economics, Democracy, Peace), which are also the phone view. Further values (0-2) are secondary traditions: seam entries are drawn on the border with the first one, and they feed the tradition x tradition bridge matrix. Rows of the field x problem matrix. Generalist funders keep a nominal home but sit in a funder band outside the wedges with spokes to their secondary traditions, excluded from sector counts.

categories.label: Formal & physical sciences
categories.definition: Wheel 1 (Sciences & engineering). Mathematics, theoretical physics and CS, logic, decision and game theory as foundations for understanding and aligning AI: singular learning theory, computational mechanics, category theory and verification, algorithmic information theory, agent foundations, game theory of cooperation, bargaining and races.
categories.boundary: Complexity, cybernetics and agent-based models go to Life & systems (B6); safety cases to Safety; game theory of markets or power to Economics.

categories.label: Life & systems sciences
categories.definition: Wheel 2 (Sciences & engineering). Sciences of living and self-organising wholes: evolutionary and developmental biology, basal and collective intelligence, artificial life; neuroscience, NeuroAI, active inference, brain emulation; complexity; cybernetics, systems science, ecology, resilience; the systems strand of metacrisis thinking.
categories.boundary: Experience or moral status of AI goes to AI minds (B4); experiments on models to Psychology (B5); proofs to Formal (B6); metamodern work to Contemplative (B7).

categories.label: Consciousness & AI minds
categories.definition: Wheel 3 (Minds & inner life). Consciousness science, sentience science and philosophy of mind applied to whether AI (and animals) have experience, welfare or moral status: indicators, welfare assessments, digital-minds field-building and governance, animal sentience bridged to AI, relational study of model minds.
categories.boundary: Clinical work on mind attribution goes to Psychology (B3); ethics with AI welfare as one strand to Philosophy (B13); AI-rights law to Law; Buddhist accounts of mind to Contemplative.

categories.label: Psychology & cognitive science
categories.definition: Wheel 4 (Minds & inner life). Clinical psychology, psychiatry, psychoanalysis and peer support; child development; social, moral and wisdom psychology; relationships and affect; computational cognitive science and machine psychology; and coaching and applied-rationality services for AI-safety workers.
categories.boundary: Neuroscience goes to Life & systems (B5); meditation and compassion practice to Contemplative (B2); children's-rights law to Law (B9); AI consciousness to AI minds (B3).

categories.label: Contemplative & integral traditions
categories.definition: Wheel 5 (Minds & inner life). First-person, practice-based traditions and their science: meditation and contemplative training, contemplative and compassion science, contemplative insight turned into AI design or alignment targets, and the integral, metamodern and inner-development milieu int/a comes from.
categories.boundary: Bodies speaking for a religious tradition, incl. Buddhist federations, translation, media and funders, go to Religion (B1); empirical wellbeing research and field-health services to Psychology (B2).

categories.label: Religion & theology
categories.definition: Wheel 6 (Minds & inner life). Organisations that speak from, for or to a religious tradition: churches, denominations, federations, interfaith bodies; theology, religious studies and religious law; faith media, investors, benchmarks and advocacy; chaplaincy; faith and science-and-religion funders.
categories.boundary: Contemplative practice or AI artefacts built from contemplative insight go to Contemplative (B1); religious-founded peace research to Peace (B11); ADL to Law.

categories.label: Philosophy & ethics
categories.definition: Wheel 7 (Humanities & cultures). Moral and political philosophy (longtermist, suffering-focused, virtue, care ethics), philosophy of technology and intelligence, continental and process thought, Chinese and African academic philosophy, applied ethics, bioethics and ethics councils.
categories.boundary: Philosophy of mind mainly about AI consciousness goes to AI minds (B13); theology to Religion; metamodern philosophy to Contemplative.

categories.label: Arts, narrative & futures
categories.definition: Wheel 8 (Humanities & cultures). Imaginative and anticipatory disciplines: art, design and speculative design; narrative, literary and cultural studies; film, games, journalism and communications; futures studies and foresight (scenarios, Delphi, horizon scanning, wargames, technology assessment), incl. stories as model priors.
categories.boundary: STS goes to Law; decolonial speculative work to Indigenous; probabilistic forecasting to Democracy (B10); a community's publication to that community (H3).

categories.label: Indigenous & decolonial knowledges
categories.definition: Wheel 9 (Humanities & cultures). Indigenous knowledge systems and data sovereignty (kinship ontologies, tikanga and kaitiakitanga, CARE principles, TK labels, Ubuntu-guided research) and decolonial, Black and feminist standpoint traditions that rebuild AI from marginalised communities' knowledge.
categories.boundary: Knowledge tradition, not geography (B8): Global South or feminist groups working through law, policy, economics or civic tech go to those sectors; location shows in region and standpoint.

categories.label: Law, rights & society
categories.definition: Wheel 10 (Society & institutions). Law and legal theory (liability, human, children's and digital rights, whistleblowing, AI-rights advocacy), STS, sociology, anthropology, critical data studies, civil-society auditing, and public-interest, ELSI and development research and funding.
categories.boundary: Labour, competition and political economy go to Economics (B9); deliberation to Democracy; humanitarian law to Peace; certification to Safety.

categories.label: Economics, labour & commons
categories.definition: Wheel 11 (Society & institutions). Economics of transformative AI (growth, labour, public finance, cash transfers), political economy and antitrust (power concentration, lock-in), commons, cooperatives and public-goods governance, and organised labour, incl. data workers.
categories.boundary: Game theory of AI agents goes to Formal; process design to Democracy; workers' rights as human rights to Law; complex-systems disempowerment work to Life & systems.

categories.label: Democracy & collective intelligence
categories.definition: Wheel 12 (Society & institutions). Deliberative and participatory democracy (assemblies, deliberative polling, sortition, broad listening), collective-intelligence science and AI-for-democracy tools, and collective epistemics: forecasting, argument mapping, fact-checking, provenance, knowledge commons.
categories.boundary: Peacebuilders' deliberative tools go to Peace (B11); mechanism design to Economics; foresight to Arts (B10); rights advocacy to Law.

categories.label: Peace, security & diplomacy
categories.definition: Wheel 13 (Society & institutions). Nuclear risk and arms control, security studies and humanitarian law, Track II, science and multilateral diplomacy (incl. China studies), and peacebuilding, mediation and conflict transformation applied to AI and the AI race.
categories.boundary: Biosecurity and catastrophe resilience go to Safety (B12); interfaith ethics statements to Religion; information integrity to Democracy unless framed as security.

categories.label: Safety & risk sciences
categories.definition: Wheel 14 (Sciences & engineering), closing on Formal via verification. Safety-critical engineering and assurance (STAMP/STPA, safety cases, certification, standards), human factors, resilience engineering, incident reporting, risk management, insurance, infosec, catastrophe resilience, public health and biosecurity.
categories.boundary: Verification as mathematics goes to Formal; nonproliferation diplomacy to Peace (B12); rights auditing to Law.

facets.name: Sub-tradition
facets.question: Within its home tradition, which recognisable school or community is it part of?
facets.role_in_ui: Slices inside each wedge at zoom, and a filter. Keeps contrasts a wedge average hides: in Life & systems the cybernetics slice is 0 core / 3 bridge / 4 adjacent / 7 potential while NeuroAI is 5 / 4 / 0 / 3. Choose only within the entry's home (key prefix).

facets.name: Ring of proximity
facets.question: How close is it to the AI-safety core?
facets.role_in_ui: Concentric rings, core at the centre. Rings mean proximity, not developmental height or value; the potential ring gets full visual weight. Classic-map status is a separate dot fill. Pre-filled from the roster; profilers verify with the guide's decision tree.

categories.label: AI-safety core
categories.definition: Making advanced AI go well (alignment, safety, catastrophic or existential risk, AI welfare, governance of transformative AI) is the organisation's founding or primary mission; it belongs to the AI-safety and x-risk ecosystem (funded by, staffed from or listed by that community, often on the aisafety.com map); and it imports knowledge or methods from outside mainstream ML alignment and conventional AI policy. Includes AI-safety programmes inside frontier labs and national AI-safety institutes.
categories.boundary: Being on the aisafety.com map is a separate facet. An older institution from another field that opened an AI-safety programme is bridge however large the programme (SIPRI, York CfAA). A new organisation founded by people from another field whose founding mission is AI safety is core (Simplex, Softmax, Eleos).

categories.label: Bridge from elsewhere
categories.definition: Rooted in another field or tradition (its people, institution, funding or identity belong there) and running a sustained, explicit programme on AI safety, catastrophic or existential risk, alignment, superintelligence, AI welfare or 'AI going well'. Sustained means a standing programme, funded project, fellowship, publication line or repeated convening in 2024-26, not a single event.
categories.boundary: AI work on present harms with no safety, catastrophic-risk, alignment or 'going well' framing is adjacent. A single talk, essay or workshop is potential.

categories.label: Adjacent, no x-risk frame
categories.definition: Has a sustained AI programme rooted in another tradition, focused on AI's human, societal or cultural effects (harms, rights, wellbeing, labour, meaning, democracy, religion), without catastrophic-risk, alignment or 'AI going well' framing.
categories.boundary: If it starts framing its work around catastrophic risk, alignment or AI welfare, it moves to bridge. If its AI engagement is light (events, essays, one study), it is potential.

categories.label: Potential partner
categories.definition: Holds highly relevant knowledge, methods or reach, but its AI engagement is light (occasional events, essays, a single paper or session) or absent. The profiler must name, in one line, the transferable method that justifies inclusion.
categories.boundary: Once it runs a standing AI programme it moves to adjacent or bridge. Empty or thin potential cells may be search artefacts (English-only search, exhausted search budgets, no sweep of statistics, operations research or logic) and are labelled as such on the map.

facets.name: Problem addressed
facets.question: Which parts of 'making the transition to advanced AI go well' does its work bear on? (1-3 values; the first is the primary problem.)
facets.role_in_ui: Columns of the field x problem matrix, grouped into four arcs (The AI itself; Human minds & meaning; Living & deciding together; Cooperation, conflict & civilisation). The arc of the first (primary) value is the mandala's default colour, four hues. Multi-valued because single-label field and problem are strongly correlated and would collapse the matrix onto its diagonal; the second value is shown as the 'second-best' placement in the detail panel.

categories.label: Understanding AI & agency
categories.definition: [The AI itself] A scientific or formal account of what AI systems are and do: how goals, agency, learning, world-models and capabilities arise, interpretability from physics, neuroscience, biology or cognitive science, and how agents could be designed differently.
categories.boundary: Moral status, values, testing deployed systems and many-agent dynamics have their own columns.

categories.label: What AI should value
categories.definition: [The AI itself] The alignment target: which values, virtues, wisdom, care or character AI should have, and how to specify, train or evaluate for them from moral, contemplative, religious, Indigenous, developmental or narrative traditions.
categories.boundary: Addressing people about dignity, not models, is Meaning; add Democratic voice when public input yields a model spec.

categories.label: Assurance & oversight
categories.definition: [The AI itself] Making specific AI systems demonstrably safe and overseeable: evals and red-teaming, verification and safety cases, certification and standards, audits, incident reporting, human factors of oversight, insurance of deployed systems.
categories.boundary: Internals go to Agency; liability to Rights; misuse by states to Security; recovery to Systemic risk.

categories.label: Moral status of AI
categories.definition: [The AI itself] Whether AI systems are or could be subjects whose experiences matter, and what relationship follows: consciousness indicators, welfare assessments, digital-minds governance, relational study of model minds, AI-rights advocacy.
categories.boundary: Harm to humans from mind attribution is Protecting minds (code both if both).

categories.label: Protecting minds & relationships
categories.definition: [Human minds & meaning] What AI does to human minds, development and relationships: companion harms, AI-associated psychosis and dependency, children's development, attention and cognitive liberty, manipulation and emulated empathy, sycophancy as harm, people's own agency.
categories.boundary: Meaning goes to Meaning; AI-safety workers to People; information integrity to Sensemaking.

categories.label: Meaning, dignity & formation
categories.definition: [Human minds & meaning] Humanity's moral and spiritual orientation to AI: what it means to be human, dignity and flourishing, moral and character formation, and the ethical voice of religious, humanist and contemplative communities to their members and publics.
categories.boundary: Insight turned into model specs is What AI should value; red lines go to Rights or Security.

categories.label: People doing the work
categories.definition: [Human minds & meaning] The people who build, govern, fund and make AI safe: wellbeing, inner development, practical wisdom, conscience, oaths, whistleblowing, worker voice in labs, and the data-labelling and rating workforce; also widening who does this work.
categories.boundary: Public mental health is Protecting minds; labour as counter-power is Power.

categories.label: Sensemaking, truth & foresight
categories.definition: [Living & deciding together] Whether people and institutions can see clearly with AI: forecasting, foresight and early warning, reasoning tools, model truthfulness, fact-checking, provenance, epistemic commons, information integrity, and how publics picture and narrate AI futures.
categories.boundary: Deciding together is Democratic voice; individual cognitive harm is Protecting minds.

categories.label: Democratic voice & legitimacy
categories.definition: [Living & deciding together] How societies decide together about and with AI: assemblies and sortition, deliberative polling, public input into model behaviour, AI-assisted deliberation and bridging, collective intelligence, civil liberties, polycentric governance.
categories.boundary: Facts and forecasts are Sensemaking; legal accountability is Rights.

categories.label: Rights & plural voices
categories.definition: [Living & deciding together] Whose interests and voices count, and how developers are held to account: human-rights and liability law, bias and accountability audits, data and cultural sovereignty, Indigenous rights, Global South voice, feminist and decolonial alternatives.
categories.boundary: Participation procedures are Democratic voice; competition and labour are Power.

categories.label: Power, wealth & work
categories.definition: [Living & deciding together] Who holds power and wealth as AI takes over labour and judgement: concentration and lock-in, gradual disempowerment, windfall distribution and TAI economics, competition policy, public AI, data ownership, labour as counter-power.
categories.boundary: Litigation for specific harms is Rights; data-worker wellbeing is People.

categories.label: Multi-agent AI & cooperation
categories.definition: [Cooperation, conflict & civilisation] Populations of interacting AI agents and the cooperation science that governs them: cooperative AI, collusion, bargaining and commitment, emergent collective behaviour, multi-agent security, game-theoretic models of AI races.
categories.boundary: Rivalry of states or labs studied diplomatically is Security.

categories.label: Security & international coordination
categories.definition: [Cooperation, conflict & civilisation] Keeping states, militaries and developers from catastrophic conflict and misuse: military AI and nuclear escalation, autonomous weapons, bio and cyber misuse, influence operations, US-China and Track II dialogue, UN processes, treaties, red lines.
categories.boundary: AI-to-AI conflict is Multi-agent AI.

categories.label: Systemic risk & metacrisis
categories.definition: [Cooperation, conflict & civilisation] AI as one thread in civilisation's systemic predicament, and resilience when prevention fails: metacrisis and polycrisis, multipolar traps, planetary boundaries, catastrophe preparedness and recovery, infrastructure risk, long-term trajectory, future generations.
categories.boundary: Races with a cooperation or diplomacy programme go to Multi-agent or Security; economic disempowerment to Power.

facets.name: Integral quadrant
facets.question: Which dimensions of reality does its AI work attend to and try to change: inner experience, shared meaning, observable mechanisms, or collective systems? (1-2 values; first is main.)
facets.role_in_ui: int/a lens coded per entry from the object of the work, not derived from tradition (deriving it mislabelled CHT). Crossed with family it shows which inner (I, We) traditions reach the It of models. Switchable colour layer; plain labels lead.

categories.label: Minds & experience (I)
categories.definition: The interior of individuals: experience, wellbeing, cognition as lived, development, character, contemplative states, and the possible interiority or welfare of AI systems.
categories.boundary: Brains and behaviour observed from outside are It.

categories.label: Meaning & culture (We)
categories.definition: Shared interiors: values, ethics, religion, narratives, culture, intersubjective understanding, dialogue and deliberation as meaning-making.
categories.boundary: Formal institutions, law and markets are Its.

categories.label: Mechanisms & machines (It)
categories.definition: The observable structure and behaviour of single systems: AI models and agents (internals, behaviour, evaluations, training data), brains and organisms, engineered artefacts and their verification.
categories.boundary: Ecosystems of many agents and sociotechnical institutions are Its.

categories.label: Systems & structures (Its)
categories.definition: Collective exteriors: institutions, law, markets, geopolitics, ecosystems of interacting agents, and complex social and ecological systems.
categories.boundary: Shared meaning and dialogue are We.

facets.name: Role
facets.question: What does the organisation actually do, and how does it expect that to make a difference? (1-3 values, main first.)
facets.role_in_ui: Filter and theory-of-change lens (merges lever and activity). With problem it builds the parallel-worlds view of communities using different levers on the same problem.

categories.label: Research & theory
categories.definition: Produces original studies, theory or analysis that change what the field thinks is true or possible.
categories.boundary: Applied measurement that tracks a problem is Measure & evaluate.

categories.label: Measure & evaluate
categories.definition: Benchmarks, evals, audits, red-teaming, ratings, indices, surveys, incident databases and forecasts that make a problem visible and trackable.
categories.boundary: Building tools others use is Build.

categories.label: Build tools & alternatives
categories.definition: Software, datasets, infrastructure, prototypes, products or alternative AI systems that embody a different way of doing things.
categories.boundary: Standards that others must meet are Set norms & standards.

categories.label: Set norms & standards
categories.definition: Principles, codes, technical standards, certification, design codes, labels, professional oaths and religious rulings that define acceptable practice.
categories.boundary: Binding law, litigation and regulation are Law, policy & advocacy.

categories.label: Law, policy & advocacy
categories.definition: Litigation, legislation, regulatory advice, treaty campaigns and advocacy aimed at governments or courts.
categories.boundary: Voluntary codes are Set norms & standards; mass participation is Widen participation.

categories.label: Convene & mediate
categories.definition: Dialogues, Track II channels, summits, conferences, workshops and brokering that build trust or shared understanding between groups that do not otherwise meet.
categories.boundary: Structured processes that hand decisions to citizens are Widen participation.

categories.label: Widen participation
categories.definition: Participatory, deliberative or sovereignty-based processes that give affected or excluded people real say.
categories.boundary: Elite expert dialogue is Convene & mediate.

categories.label: Organise collective power
categories.definition: Unions, coalitions, campaigns, movements and shareholder action that put collective pressure on developers or governments.
categories.boundary: Policy advice from a single organisation is Law, policy & advocacy.

categories.label: Educate & form
categories.definition: Courses, schools, fellowships with teaching, trainings, retreats and character or contemplative formation that change people's capacities.
categories.boundary: One-off events are Convene; funding-only fellowships are Fund.

categories.label: Care & support
categories.definition: Direct psychological, spiritual, peer, coaching or legal support to individuals.
categories.boundary: Research about wellbeing is Research.

categories.label: Media, art & storytelling
categories.definition: Journalism, publishing, newsletters, podcasts, film, art, scenarios and serious games for public or decision-maker audiences.
categories.boundary: Calibrated numerical forecasts are Measure & evaluate.

categories.label: Fund others
categories.definition: Grants, fellowships, prizes and pooled funds that resource other organisations.
categories.boundary: An organisation that mainly does the work and funds a little on the side is classed by what it does.

facets.name: Organisation type
facets.question: What kind of organisation is the roster entry?
facets.role_in_ui: Filter and dot shape; separates membership bodies (unions, societies, federations), which discovery under-covered, from NGOs and labs.

categories.label: Independent nonprofit
categories.definition: Independent nonprofit, charity, NGO or think tank, including independent research institutes.
categories.boundary: University units are Academic; a unit inside another organisation is Programme.

categories.label: Academic centre or lab
categories.definition: University centre, lab, institute or research group, and units of public research organisations (Max Planck, Fraunhofer, DLR).
categories.boundary: A time-limited consortium funded by a research council is Programme.

categories.label: Hosted programme or project
categories.definition: A programme, project, consortium, workshop series or strand inside a host organisation, or a time-limited funded project.
categories.boundary: A permanent centre with its own identity is Academic or Nonprofit.

categories.label: Funder or fund
categories.definition: Foundation, pooled fund, grant programme or philanthropic investor whose main AI activity is funding.
categories.boundary: An operating organisation that also gives grants is classed by its main activity.

categories.label: Network or coalition

categories.boundary: Bodies with formal members and credentials are Membership body.

categories.label: Membership body
categories.definition: Union, professional association, learned society, standards community with members, or religious denomination or federation acting for its members.
categories.boundary: Coalitions of organisations without individual members are Network.

categories.label: Company or startup
categories.definition: For-profit company, public-benefit corporation or studio.
categories.boundary: A company's nonprofit arm is Nonprofit.

categories.label: Publication or media

categories.label: Public or intergovernmental body

facets.name: Direction of transfer
facets.question: What actually flows from its tradition into the AI transition: who or what changes because of its work?
facets.role_in_ui: The sharpest int/a lens and a switchable colour layer: has a tradition reached the model or the builders, or does it still mostly talk to its own people?

categories.label: Into the model
categories.definition: The tradition's knowledge is applied to AI systems themselves: training data, internals, agent design, model specs or evaluations aimed at model behaviour.
categories.boundary: Rules for how humans govern models are Into institutions.

categories.label: Into the builders
categories.definition: The tradition's practices reach the people who build, govern or fund AI, as people: wellbeing, formation, conscience, oaths, whistleblowing support, organising inside labs.
categories.boundary: Public mental health is Protecting.

categories.label: Into institutions
categories.definition: The tradition supplies templates for governing AI: dialogues and treaties, safety cases, incident systems, liability, standards, deliberative processes, collective bargaining, policy designs.
categories.boundary: Defending the tradition's own constituency is Protecting.

categories.label: Protecting its constituency
categories.definition: The tradition studies or defends the people it already serves (children, patients, workers, believers, Indigenous communities) from AI's effects.
categories.boundary: Work that changes the model itself as its main purpose is Into the model.

categories.label: Convening its community
categories.definition: The tradition brings its own community into the AI conversation: dialogues, summits, education, literacy, media for its members.
categories.boundary: Producing a governance instrument is Into institutions.

categories.label: None yet
categories.definition: Ring = potential and no AI work at all: the tradition holds relevant knowledge that has not moved.
categories.boundary: Allowed only for potential entries with no AI activity.

facets.name: Disciplinary span
facets.question: How many traditions does it combine on purpose, and how firm is its sector placement?
facets.role_in_ui: Drawing rule: single inside the wedge, seam on the border with the first secondary tradition, hub with a halo, generalist funders in the funder band. Makes provisional placements visible.

categories.label: Single tradition
categories.definition: Rooted in one tradition; the home sector is unambiguous.
categories.boundary: A deliberate second discipline makes it a seam.

categories.label: Two traditions (seam)
categories.definition: Deliberately joins two traditions; carries the second as a secondary tradition and is drawn on the seam between the two sectors.
categories.boundary: Three or more traditions convened on purpose make an Integrative hub.

categories.label: Integrative hub
categories.definition: Convenes three or more traditions on purpose; home is the tradition its AI-relevant output draws on most.
categories.boundary: Generalist money without a disciplinary programme is Generalist funder.

categories.label: Generalist funder
categories.definition: A funder whose roster entry spans three or more traditions with no single programme holding a clear majority. Keeps a nominal home for search but is drawn in the funder band and excluded from sector counts.
categories.boundary: A funder with one disciplinary programme (Carnegie Corporation, Khyentse, Amaranth, Digital Sentience Consortium, Longview's power-concentration RFP) is Single.

facets.name: Risk framing
facets.question: How does it frame what is at stake, in its own words?
facets.role_in_ui: Filter and colour layer. Shows the safety-ethics gap, lets funders match mandates, and keeps critics and positive-vision groups on the map without a forced harm frame.

categories.label: Catastrophic or existential
categories.definition: Extreme or irreversible outcomes: loss of control, mass-casualty misuse, nuclear escalation, s-risks, or moral catastrophe at scale (including mass digital suffering).
categories.boundary: Slow erosion without a decisive catastrophe is Structural.

categories.label: Structural and gradual
categories.definition: Systemic erosion without a single catastrophe: disempowerment, lock-in, power concentration, epistemic decay, rivalrous dynamics.
categories.boundary: Concrete harms to identifiable people now are Present harms.

categories.label: Present, concrete harms
categories.definition: Harms to identifiable people or groups now: rights violations, bias, child safety, labour exploitation, psychological injury.
categories.boundary: The same harms read as signs of systemic drift are Structural.

categories.label: Flourishing and positive
categories.definition: Aspirational: what a good outcome is and how to reach it (wisdom, flourishing, care, positive futures) as the main aim.
categories.boundary: Work that mainly avoids harm, even in a hopeful tone, takes a harm framing.

categories.label: Critical or deflationary
categories.definition: Sceptical or deflationary about AI capabilities, AI consciousness or x-risk discourse itself, as its main output.
categories.boundary: Critique that serves an active harms agenda as a means takes Present harms.

facets.name: Level of the whole
facets.question: At what level does the intended change land?
facets.role_in_ui: Filter and int/a colour layer (integral scale, adapted). Surfaces the thin middle levels, the human-AI relationship and ecosystems of agents, where companion harms and collusion arise.

categories.label: Single AI system
categories.definition: A single model or agent: its internals, behaviour, character, values or possible interiority.
categories.boundary: Many interacting agents are Ecosystem.

categories.label: Ecosystem of AI agents
categories.definition: Populations of interacting AI agents and the environments they act in: cooperation, collusion, conflict, emergent collective behaviour.
categories.boundary: Races between human developers or states are Organisation or World.

categories.label: Human-AI relationship
categories.definition: The human-AI pair as the unit: companionship, attachment, augmentation, teaming, attribution of mind.
categories.boundary: Effects on a person's mind with no relational focus are Person.

categories.label: Individual person
categories.definition: Individual human minds and bodies: wellbeing, cognition, development, character, including AI-safety workers as individuals.
categories.boundary: Groups and organisations are Organisation.

categories.label: Organisation or profession
categories.definition: Labs and companies, professions, faith communities, unions, standards bodies and the AI-safety field as an organised community.
categories.boundary: Whole publics, economies and nations are Society.

categories.label: Society
categories.definition: Publics, democracies, economies, information ecosystems and national institutions.
categories.boundary: Relations between states and the long-run civilisational trajectory are World.

categories.label: World and planet
categories.definition: International order, the long-term trajectory of civilisation, the biosphere and all sentient beings.
categories.boundary: National policy is Society.

facets.name: Way of knowing
facets.question: What kind of knowledge does its main AI output contribute?
facets.role_in_ui: int/a's full-spectrum knowing made concrete; colour layer in the int/a view. Independent of tradition. With role and badges it yields the derived inner/outer layer (inner-informed outer work, inner work, integrated).

categories.label: Formal & mathematical
categories.definition: Knowledge as proof, formal model or simulation.
categories.boundary: Statistical analysis of observed data is Empirical.

categories.label: Empirical & experimental
categories.definition: Knowledge from experiment, measurement, surveys and field data.
categories.boundary: Codified practitioner know-how is Practice.

categories.label: Professional & clinical practice
categories.definition: Codified practitioner knowledge: engineering assurance, clinical care, mediation, diplomacy, facilitation, standards.
categories.boundary: First-person meditative skill is Contemplative & embodied.

categories.label: Interpretive & normative
categories.definition: Knowledge from argument, textual and legal interpretation, ethical reasoning and critique.
categories.boundary: Knowledge carried by a living community rather than by scholars is Communal.

categories.label: Contemplative & embodied
categories.definition: First-person, somatic, meditative and phenomenological knowing.
categories.boundary: Third-person science of meditators is Empirical.

categories.label: Communal & lived
categories.definition: Knowledge held by a community: Indigenous knowledge, lived experience of harm, organised workers, participatory process.
categories.boundary: Expert scholarship about a community is Interpretive.

categories.label: Imaginative & creative
categories.definition: Knowledge through art, narrative, design, scenarios and play.
categories.boundary: Probabilistic forecasts are Empirical.

facets.role_in_ui: Filter and overlay that keeps geography off the primary facet while showing the Anglophone skew in every wedge.

categories.boundary: US-registered organisations that work fully distributed are Global.

categories.boundary: Multi-city organisations go by their legal base.

categories.boundary: One-off London events do not count.

categories.boundary: Elsewhere in France is recorded by region only.

categories.boundary: Recorded talks and newsletters alone do not count.

facets.name: How to engage
facets.question: How can a person or funder get involved: work, apply, attend, join, contribute or partner?
facets.role_in_ui: Practical filter for every persona. Goes stale: needs an owner and refresh schedule.

categories.boundary: Volunteer-only groups are Open contribution.

categories.boundary: Only for entries without an AI programme (normally ring potential).

facets.role_in_ui: Filter; dormant entries appear as possibly open niches in the founder view.

categories.boundary: A finished project inside an active host is Dormant only for that project.

facets.name: int/a principle badges

categories.label: Full-spectrum knowing
categories.definition: Uses embodied, contemplative, artistic, Indigenous or experiential knowing alongside rigorous analysis, as method.
categories.boundary: Citing a tradition is not enough.

categories.label: Speed of wisdom
categories.definition: Practises explicit discernment about pace: pause or slow-technology positions, de-escalation, refusing race or power-seeking dynamics.
categories.boundary: Ordinary precaution in product regulation does not qualify.

categories.label: Decoupling & recoupling
categories.definition: Analyses AI risk on its own and also inside the wider metacrisis and its systemic interconnections.
categories.boundary: Single-domain risk analysis does not qualify.

categories.label: Fractal altruism
categories.definition: Pairs scope-sensitive ambition with local, community-rooted and intrinsic values.
categories.boundary: Global programmes with no local anchoring do not qualify.

categories.label: Inner work, outer change
categories.definition: Explicitly couples the inner development of practitioners with outer change in AI.
categories.boundary: Wellbeing services or retreats with only an AI theme do not qualify.

radial_layout.order_rationale: Clockwise wheel of intellectual kinship, so every seam is where bridges already form and chords across the wheel mark new ground. Seams: Formal|Life & systems via information theory, categorical systems and complexity (XOR, Topos); Life & systems|AI minds via the neuroscience of consciousness (Sussex, AMCS); AI minds|Psychology via mind attribution (Cambridge Digital Minds, WhenAISeemsConscious); Psychology|Contemplative via wellbeing, wisdom and compassion science and field health; Contemplative|Religion on the Buddhist boundary; Religion|Philosophy via theology and ethics; Philosophy|Arts in the humanities; Arts|Indigenous via decolonial futurism (Dreaming Beyond AI, GTDF); Indigenous|Law via data sovereignty; Law|Economics via political economy and labour rights; Economics|Democracy via commons and mechanism design (RadicalxChange, Metagov); Democracy|Peace where peacebuilders use deliberative tools (Toda, UN DPPA, Build Up); Peace|Safety via nuclear and bio security (NTI, SecureBio); Safety|Formal via verification (ARIA). The sectors form four contiguous family arcs, which are also the phone view. Drawing rules: equal angles for all 14 sectors, so density shows thinness and empty sector x ring cells are labelled blank tiles ('opening' or 'possible search artefact'); rings mean proximity, not height or value, and the potential ring gets full visual weight; filled vs hollow dots = classic-map status (derived from the roster flag on_classic_map: 60 of 552 entries are on aisafety.com); seam entries sit on the border with their first secondary tradition, hubs get a halo, the 8 generalist funders sit in an outer band with spokes to the traditions they fund. Colour = arc of the primary problem (4 hues); switchable layers: transfer, framing, quadrant, way of knowing, level. Outside the wheel, a legend of absent traditions, each marked 'searched, none found' or 'not searched': anthropology and history (present only as methods), linguistics, education, library science, accounting and audit, operations research and statistics, epidemiology of AI harms; Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Shinto and Bahá'í institutions; Sufi and Christian contemplative orders; Daoist and Confucian thought beyond Berggruen and Beijing-AISI.

matrix.why: Rows: the 14 home traditions (first tradition value) in wheel order, grouped by family. Columns: the 14 problems grouped by arc. Tradition is what an organisation brings and problem is what it works on, so the cross shows which bodies of knowledge reach which problems, and its empty cells are concrete founder openings (Religion x Power despite deep doctrine on concentrated wealth; Safety science x Protecting minds, where patient-safety and incident practice has not met companion harms; Psychology x What AI should value, the missing developmental-alignment programme; Democracy x Assurance, since nobody red-teams AI facilitators). All 1-3 problem values count (toggle: primary only), because single-label field and problem correlate strongly (NMI 0.57-0.62) and would sit on the diagonal. Cells show counts shaded by core + bridge share, filled dots for classic-map entries, and 'opening' or 'possible search artefact' labels. Clicking a cell lists entries side by side, the 'parallel worlds' view (power concentration: Formation, Longview, ACS vs Open Markets, AI Now, MIT Stone, unions; human minds: UK AISI vs APsA, Stanford Brainstorm, Human Line Project). Companion grids: tradition x tradition from secondary traditions (bridges, cross-wheel ones highlighted) and family x transfer (who reaches the model, who only convenes or protects).

final.tagging_guide:
TAGGING GUIDE v1. Read the facet definitions first; this says how to apply them, one roster entry at a time.

A. GROUND RULES
A1 Unit = the roster entry. For a unit inside a host (Anthropic Model Welfare, UK AISI's societal-resilience team) tag that unit, not the host's portfolio.
A2 Evidence = its own AI outputs in 2025-26 (roster 'what it is' and 'AI connection', then its site). Never reputation or what it 'should' do, except the one-line method required for ring = potential.
A3 Bring vs aim: tradition, sub_tradition and way_of_knowing describe what it BRINGS; problem, quadrant, level, framing and transfer describe what its AI work is ABOUT and whom it changes. Geodesic brings narrative (Arts), knows empirically and works on What AI should value.
A4 Tag 17 facets: tradition (home first, then 0-2 secondary), sub_tradition, ring, problem (1-3, primary first), quadrant (1-2), role (1-3), org_type, transfer, span, framing, level, way_of_knowing, region, standpoint, inta_hub, engagement, status; badges optional. Derived, never tagged: family (from home), problem arc (from first problem), classic-map status (roster flag).
A5 One sentence of evidence for home, ring and transfer; confidence (high/medium/low) for home and primary problem; cite the rule code when a tie-breaker decided.
A6 Never invent a category: take the closest and flag 'misfit' (feeds the gap register).

B. HOME TRADITION (first value of tradition)
List its AI outputs and which discipline's methods, concepts, people or practices produced them, then apply in order:
H1 Method over topic: a psychology lab studying religious users is Psychology; a law clinic suing over chatbot harms is Law.
H2 Imported concepts: ML, AI governance and policy analysis are not sectors; if they are its own method, place it by the outside tradition whose concepts it imports (Geodesic Arts, TruthfulAI Philosophy, AE Studio Life & systems, KIRA Economics).
H3 Constituency: publications, professional bodies, unions and federations go with the community they serve (Bulletin Peace, Tricycle Religion, Integral Life Contemplative, APA Psychology, unions Economics, Digital Minds Newsletter AI minds); general-audience journalism, film and campaigns go to Arts.
H4 Funders: one-programme funders go to that programme's tradition (Carnegie Corporation Peace, Amaranth Life & systems, Khyentse Religion). Generalist funders (rule K) get a nominal home from the most distinctive line in their entry and are drawn in the funder band.
H5 Hubs: the tradition its AI output draws on most; if tied, its leadership's discipline.
Then the boundary rules, which override first instinct:
B1 Religion vs Contemplative (Buddhist test): speaking from, for or to a tradition's texts, institutions or community (federations, translation, faith media and funders, rulings, convening a faith community) is Religion: Buddhism & AI Initiative, 84000, Mindstream, WFB. A research or design artefact built from contemplative insight, or practice training for AI people regardless of faith, is Contemplative: CSAS, Arising, Mathematical Metaphysics Institute, FLIP, MAPLE, Wisdom + AI. Integral, metamodern and Teilhardian bodies are Contemplative.
B2 Psychology vs Contemplative: third-person wisdom, flourishing or wellbeing research is Psychology (Wisdom and Culture Lab, Greater Good); meditation-based training and contemplative science are Contemplative (CCARE, Garrison). Services for AI-safety workers (CFAR, ESPR, Rethink Wellbeing, Upgradable) are Psychology unless they are contemplative practice (MAPLE).
B3 Psychology vs AI minds: people attributing minds to AI, clinical lens Psychology (Human Line Project), led by consciousness or welfare researchers AI minds (WhenAISeemsConscious, Cambridge Digital Minds).
B4 Life & systems vs AI minds: neuroscience used to build or read AI is Life & systems; asking whether AI or animals have experience is AI minds, whatever the method (Sussex).
B5 Life & systems vs Psychology: brains and organisms Life & systems; cognitive science and experiments on models Psychology (Re-Align, IRIS, Helmholtz Munich).
B6 Formal vs Life & systems: proofs and mathematical theory of learning and agents Formal (Iliad, Simplex, CAIF, CLR); complexity, emergence, agent-based simulation, cybernetics Life & systems (XOR Labs, ACS, Concordia).
B7 Metacrisis: systems diagnosis Life & systems (Consilience, Club of Rome, Game B); inner-development or metamodern method Contemplative (Perspectiva, Life Itself, IDG).
B8 Indigenous & decolonial vs Law, Economics, Democracy: knowledge tradition, not geography or identity. Indigenous-led knowledge and data sovereignty, or decolonial, Black or feminist epistemology as the core contribution, stay (Te Hiku, GIDA, DAIR); rights law, policy, advocacy, political economy or civic tech by Global South or feminist groups go to those sectors (GCG, IT for Change, SUPERRR, Tattle), with location in region and standpoint.
B9 Law vs Economics vs Psychology: power, competition, labour and commons Economics; rights, liability, audits, STS, ELSI Law; children's-rights law Law, child-development science Psychology; AI-rights advocacy argued as law Law.
B10 Democracy vs Arts: probabilistic forecasting, argument mapping, fact-checking Democracy; scenarios, foresight, wargames, technology assessment Arts.
B11 Democracy vs Peace: deliberative tools used by peacebuilders in conflict settings, and religious-founded peace research, are Peace (Toda, UN DPPA, CMI).
B12 Safety vs Peace: biosecurity evaluation, health security, catastrophe resilience Safety; nonproliferation and arms control Peace.
B13 Philosophy vs AI minds: philosophy of mind mainly about AI consciousness AI minds (Essentia); moral philosophy with AI welfare as one strand Philosophy (CRS). Ethics councils Philosophy.

C. SECONDARY TRADITIONS: after the home, 0-2 values (3 for hubs; up to 4 for generalist funders, listing what they fund most), only for methods, staff or formal partners, never mere topic, never ML or AI policy. For a seam entry the first secondary value is the seam it is drawn on.
D. SUB-TRADITION: only among the home's sub-traditions (key prefix = home); if two fit, the one matching its main AI output.
E. RING: keep the roster value unless evidence contradicts it; say why if you change it. (1) Founding or primary mission is making advanced AI go well, inside the AI-safety/x-risk ecosystem: core. (2) Otherwise no sustained AI programme in 2024-26 (standing programme, funded project, fellowship, publication line, repeated convening): potential. (3) Programme explicitly framed around safety, catastrophic risk, alignment, superintelligence, AI welfare or 'AI going well': bridge; else adjacent. Old institutions with new AI-safety programmes are bridge however large; new AI-safety organisations founded by people from other fields are core.
F. PROBLEM: primary first (test: if it vanished, which column loses most?); others only for sustained lines of work. Must-pair: values + democracy when public input yields a model spec (CIP, MAI); minds + ai_status when work spans attribution and welfare; assurance + the substantive problem when it builds evaluations (CEFEAI, Common Sense). Funders: the problems of the work they fund.
G. QUADRANT: the object of the work, never the home. Single AI systems, brains, artefacts It; many agents, institutions, markets, geopolitics, ecologies Its; experience, wellbeing, character, possible AI interiority I; values, meaning, culture, narrative, religion, dialogue We. 1-2, main first; 3-4 only for explicitly integral frameworks. FLIP It+I; CEFEAI It+We; Formation Its; CHT Its+I.
H. ROLE: 1-3 by share of effort. Fund only if it gives money to others; Educate needs teaching or formation (events alone are Convene).
I. ORG TYPE: units inside hosts Programme; university units and public research institutes Academic; unions, societies, denominations, federations Membership body; agencies, statutory councils, UN/OECD/OIC bodies, AI-safety institutes Public body.
J. TRANSFER: 'who or what changes because of this work?' First that fits its PRIMARY purpose: (1) AI systems: Into the model; (2) the people who build, govern or fund AI, as people: Into the builders; (3) governance instruments: Into institutions; (4) its own constituency protected from AI: Protecting; (5) its own community informed and convened: Convening; (6) ring potential with no AI work at all: None yet, never otherwise. Common Sense Media's ratings exist to protect children, so Protecting. Funders: the work they fund.
K. SPAN: traditions used on purpose (ML and AI policy do not count): one Single, two Seam, three or more Hub. Generalist funder = a funder spanning three or more traditions with no majority programme; in v1 exactly FLI, Coefficient Giving, SFF, Schmidt Sciences, OpenAI Foundation, CIFAR, Humanity AI, JTF Future of Intelligence. Flag any other candidate.
L. FRAMING: its own dominant statement of stakes; prefer the mission statement. Harm documentation Present harms (AlgorithmWatch); critique of capabilities, AI consciousness or x-risk discourse as main output Critical (DAIR, Sussex). Mass digital suffering is Catastrophic.
M. LEVEL: AI-safety workers as individuals are Person; labs, professions, faith communities, unions and the AI-safety field are Organisation.
N. WAY OF KNOWING: the kind of knowledge its main AI output is; independent of home. Funders: what the funded work produces.
O. PRACTICAL: region by headquarters, Global only without a base. Standpoint Majority World if led from or centred on Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, South, Southeast or Central Asia, MENA or the Pacific Islands (China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore Neither in v1); a Northern host's programme only if led locally. Hub: office, team or at least quarterly in-person activity; Online if a recurring programme can be joined remotely. Engagement only from its own 2025-26 site; Door to open only without an AI programme. Status Dormant covers closed, maintenance mode and lapsed sites.
P. BADGES (int/a view only): clear exemplars, at most two per entry, about one entry in ten overall.

Q. WORKED EXAMPLES (home+secondary | sub | ring | problems | quadrant | role | type | transfer | span | framing | level | knowing)
1 Monash M3CS: contemplative (B1, B4: 'Contemplative AI' is a design proposal from contemplative insight), minds, life | cont_science | bridge | values, ai_status | It, I | research | academic | into_model | hub | flourishing | ai_system | empirical.
2 Geodesic Research: arts (H2) | arts_narrative | core | values, agency | It, We | research | nonprofit | into_model | single | catastrophic | ai_system | empirical.
3 Buddhism & AI Initiative: religion (B1), contemplative | rel_buddhist | bridge | meaning, values | We | convene, educate | network | convening | seam | flourishing | organisation | interpretive. Contrast CSAS: contemplative (B1: 'Building Bodhisattvas' is an alignment-target model), life | cont_science | bridge | values, agency | It, I | research | nonprofit | into_model | seam | flourishing | ai_system | interpretive; standpoint majority_world.

final.rationale:
Base: the disciplines designer's 14-sector Traditions Wheel and kinship order, which both judges ranked strongest. Tradition is the unit the brief names (adjacent fields), the first question outsiders ask, independent of proximity (so empty sector x ring cells mean something) and robust (three independent field schemes agreed on 78-86% of placements). Problem stays a full, many-valued second axis rather than the primary facet, because as a primary facet it partly encoded proximity and drifted back to AI safety's own agenda terms.

Edits. (1) Consciousness & AI minds gets its own wedge (Judge 1, integral and navigator designers): 25 entries, 7 core / 14 bridge / 2 adjacent / 2 potential, none on the classic map. (2) Formal stays separate from Life & systems (Judge 2): an absorbed core, 16/5/0/2, 12 of 23 on the map. (3) To stay at 14 without merging Formal into complexity, neuroscience and NeuroAI join Life & systems and cognitive science and machine psychology join Psychology; the cybernetics & systems slice still shows the unmet systems tradition int/a names (0/3/4/7, none on the map) beside NeuroAI (5/4/0/3). (4) Indigenous & decolonial stays a knowledge-tradition sector (both judges) with a tighter test that moves IT for Change, SUPERRR and Tattle out; its 13 entries are 0/0/12/1, the clearest empty cells; a standpoint facet shows Majority-World work in every wedge. (5) Eight generalist funders leave the wedges for a funder band (designers put Schmidt and CIFAR in three different sectors); with FLI out, Religion's core is empty (0/12/26/6). (6) Field-health services stay in Psychology, so Contemplative honestly shows one core entry (Groundless Alignment). (7) 'Method, not topic' gets a workable rule for ML-method organisations: place by imported concepts. (8) Secondary traditions are folded into the main facet (first value = home), satisfying 'single home plus optional secondary' in one place.

Balance (re-sorted from the disciplines designer's single-coder assignments, so provisional; 544 entries in wedges plus 8 funders): Formal 23, Life & systems 48, AI minds 25, Psychology 47, Contemplative 38, Religion 44, Philosophy 36, Arts 39, Indigenous 13, Law 52, Economics 43, Democracy 54, Peace 43, Safety 39 (2.4-9.9%). Core/bridge/adjacent/potential: Life & systems 13/10/7/18, Psychology 6/14/21/6, Contemplative 1/11/13/13, Philosophy 9/7/16/4, Arts 6/14/12/7, Law 2/14/34/2, Economics 5/9/27/2, Democracy 12/13/22/7, Peace 7/19/11/5, Safety 4/16/11/8. By family, classic-map share and core share: Sciences & engineering 21% and 30%, Humanities & cultures 12% and 17%, Society & institutions 9% and 14%, Minds & inner life 3% and 9%: the integral designer's headline gradient in plain labels.

Grafts. Disciplines: sub-tradition, secondary traditions with seams and a bridge matrix, span, way of knowing, transfer (latent restricted to none_yet; new 'into the builders' value), the absent-traditions legend. Problems: the problem facet nearly verbatim, with cooperation split into multi-agent AI and security, assurance separated from systemic risk, futures folded into sensemaking, four arcs as default colour; risk framing; lever merged into role. Integral: families as plain quarters and phone view, proximity-not-height, level of the whole, sparse badges for the int/a view, and a quadrant coded per entry from the object of the work (deriving it from field mislabelled CHT); stages, lines, states and types stay out. Navigator: engagement, status, region, int/a hubs, classic-map overlay, persona views.

Buildability: 17 tagged facets, most factual or nested; family, problem arc and classic-map status are derived; badges optional. All exemplar ids were checked against the roster; home and sub-tradition exemplars match the re-sorted assignment and ring exemplars match roster rings. Working files: <scratchpad>/synth/ (home.json holds the re-sorted home assignment for all 552 entries; final_trim.json is this taxonomy).
final.open_questions:
1. Untested placements: neuroscience/NeuroAI in Life & systems and cognitive science/machine psychology in Psychology (23 entries). Double-code them first; if agreement is poor, fall back to Judge 1's cut (Formal & complexity; Life & brain).
2. AI minds is partly object-defined, so its matrix row sits on Moral status of AI by construction; secondary problem values carry the information.
3. Reliability is unmeasured: designers shared one 'field lens' column (inflating 78-86% agreement), and level, quadrant and way of knowing have never been coded at scale. Publish kappa (guide section R) before the map.
4. Generalist-funder edge cases: Humanity AI and JTF are judgement calls; Omidyar, Mozilla and Current AI are treated as single-tradition Economics.
5. Standpoint: whether China (and Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore) should count as Majority World is int/a's call; it changes how Beijing-AISI, Concordia AI and the Tsinghua and Fudan centres read.
6. Geodesic in Arts rests on the imported-concepts rule (H2), which Judge 2 disputed; it can be reversed in one place.
7. Search artefacts: thin potential rings (Formal, Law, Economics, AI minds: 2 each) and absent traditions may reflect English-only search, exhausted search budgets and no sweep of statistics, operations research or logic, while religion, labour, futures and membership bodies had dedicated sweeps. Sector sizes are not field sizes; each empty cell needs a 'searched / not searched' flag.
8. Engagement and status go stale and need an owner; the navigator's maturity facet is deferred until the roster has founding dates and staff counts.
9. Display tests: sub-tradition slices by default or on zoom; legibility of 14 equal sectors at phone width (fallback: families); showing a 13-entry wedge beside 54-entry wedges without implying rank.
10. 'Should engage' for potential entries is the softest ring call; the required one-line method makes it auditable, not objective.

designs.reveals:
1. The AI-safety core draws on only a few traditions. Four sectors (formal sciences, living and complex systems, mind and brain, democracy and collective intelligence) hold 49 of the 94 core entries. Formal sciences is the extreme case: 16 of 23 entries are core, 12 are on the classic map, none are adjacent, and only two are potential (Simons Physics of Learning, Basis). Its outside world has largely been pulled into the core through the Alignment Project, ARIA and Iliad. Other traditions have barely been reached. Contemplative has 1 core entry out of 37 (Groundless Alignment). Religion's only core entry is FLI, a funder. Indigenous and decolonial has no core and no bridge entries at all. Law has 3 core out of 53.

2. The classic map has met only some traditions. Only 60 of 552 entries are on aisafety.com. That includes none of the 37 contemplative entries, none of the 16 Indigenous and decolonial entries, 2 of 46 in religion (Buddhism and AI Initiative, FLI) and 2 of 42 in economics. Psychology is the telling case. Its four entries on the classic map are UK AISI plus three services that care for safety workers (Rethink Wellbeing, Upgradable, AI Safety Support). The map knows psychology as care for the field, not as knowledge about what AI does to people's minds and relationships. That knowledge sits in 20 adjacent entries: AIPRC, Stanford Brainstorm, APsA, Turkle, Kinsey and others.

3. The empty and sparse cells point to specific gaps:
- **Indigenous and decolonial, core and bridge rings: empty.** Indigenous data governance (the CARE principles, the Kaitiakitanga Licence, Local Contexts' TK labels, Māori algorithmic sovereignty) already answers training-data consent and provenance questions, but no Indigenous-led group engages frontier alignment.
- **Law and economics: mostly adjacent.** These traditions are busy with AI but rarely with catastrophic or loss-of-control questions. Law has 34 adjacent entries against 3 core. Economics has 26 adjacent against 5 core. Of 13 labour bodies, only one is a bridge (UTAW's union campaign at Google DeepMind). No union frames gradual disempowerment as a loss of human bargaining power.

4. Two sectors hold large reserves of relevant knowledge that is not yet engaged. Living and complex systems has 15 potential entries: the cybernetics and systems societies (ASC, the UK Cybernetics Society, ISSS, System Dynamics Society), the Bateson Institute, ISAL, CASCB, the Cultural Evolution Society, Cascade and Game B. That is exactly the 'systems thinking' int/a names, and almost none of it touches AI control. Contemplative and integral has 13 potential entries (IDG, Presencing, the Mindfulness Initiative, Garrison, Life Itself, Metamoderna, The Stoa, IEC, Esalen and others), so int/a's own milieu has mostly not turned to AI yet.

5. Two traditions show what a mature bridge looks like. Mind and brain has 21 bridge entries out of 39: neuroscience and consciousness science built their own institutions (the Amaranth NeuroAI roadmap, Eleos, PRISM, Sussex, the Digital Sentience Consortium). Peace has 20 bridges, from nuclear risk and Track II diplomacy. These are templates for other traditions.

6. The funding is in the wrong places for int/a's traditions. None of the 33 funders sits in the contemplative or Indigenous sectors. The big new non-EA pools sit in law and economics: Humanity AI ($500M), EAISF, Omidyar, Mozilla, Current AI ($400M+) and IDRC AI4D. Templeton money (JTF's $60M Intelligence venture, TWCF's Diverse Intelligences hubs) sits in religion and systems without a safety framing. So the 'new funders' Patrick mentions are funding traditions that rarely use x-risk framing. Translating between them is an open role for int/a.

7. The wheel order shows where bridges form, and where they don't. Most bridges cross to a neighbouring sector:
- mind and contemplative: Monash M3CS, FLIP, QRI
- formal and systems: XOR, Simplex, Topos
- democracy and peace: UN DPPA, Toda, CMI and Build Up, using deliberative tools in conflict settings
- safety and formal: verification

Bridges across the wheel are rare and are where new work could start. Religion has reached models only through representation benchmarks (CEFEAI, the AI Christian Benchmark, Gloo FAI). Contemplative reaches formal only through the Mathematical Metaphysics Institute. Indigenous reaches nothing in the core.

8. Some disciplines have no sector at all, which is itself a gap:
- Anthropology appears only as a method (Data & Society, Equiano's ethnography).
- History appears only through CAPAS and Formation's entrenchment research.
- Linguistics appears only through Masakhane and ARG-tech.
- Education and pedagogy appear only through Nordic Bildung, ESPR and Digital Thriving.
- Nobody does epidemiology of AI harms.
- No immunology-inspired defence organisation exists.
- Library and information science appears only through Wikimedia.
- There are no accounting or audit bodies and no operations research.
- Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Shinto and Bahá'í institutions are absent.
- Daoist and Confucian thought appears only through Berggruen and Beijing-AISI.
- Christian contemplative and Sufi traditions appear almost nowhere (Kosmos only).

Each of these is a concrete opening for a founder.

9. A first pass on the transfer facet suggests where the white space is. The human and inner traditions mostly convene their own communities or protect their own constituencies. Few put their methods into the model itself: wisdom and discernment evaluations, contemplative interpretability experiments, and socioaffective alignment evaluations built with clinicians are mostly missing.

designs.reveals:
1. The human-facing problems have hollow cores. Meaning has 0 core entries out of 50, and none are on the classic map. Minds has 1 core entry out of 44: UK AISI's societal-resilience team, which is also its only classic-map entry. Justice has 3 core out of 51 (ILINA, ORCG, KIRA) and 2 on the map. Democracy has 5 core out of 42 and only 2 on the map (AOI and Odyssean); CIP, Polis and Stanford DDL are missing although they run processes with frontier labs. Agency, by contrast, has 18 core entries and 13 on the map. The widening the AI-safety field has already done is mostly "other sciences into technical alignment" (Princint, Iliad, ARIA, Simplex), not "other fields into the human side of the problem".

2. A whole field is missing from the classic map. The AI-minds sector holds 33 entries, 8 of them core (Eleos, Rethink Priorities' Digital Consciousness Model, PRISM, the Digital Sentience Consortium, Anthropic Model Welfare, CRS, Cyborgism, the Digital Minds Newsletter). None appears in the scraped aisafety.com map. Inside the sector, an EA welfare wing and a relational wing (Anima Labs, Arising, Gesturing Towards Decolonial Futures, Abundant Intelligences, Aarhus Robophilosophy, Signal Front) barely meet. Both are separate from the minds sector, which studies the same phenomenon, people attributing minds to AI, from the harm side.

3. Some outer rings are empty, which is where adjacent knowledge goes unused. The potential ring holds 1 entry in power (OpenResearch), 2 in justice, 2 in target and 2 in AI minds. In power, the people who know how states behave when citizens' labour stops mattering are absent from the roster altogether: resource-curse and rentier-state economists, sovereign-wealth experts, historians of state formation, constitutional scholars. Longview's power-concentration RFP explicitly asks for that analysis. In target, the missing holders are comparative ethicists, developmental psychologists (Kegan, Gilligan lineages) and moral-education bodies who could review model specifications. The opposite holds for metacrisis, int/a's home framing: 13 of its 28 entries are potential. Those organisations have the theory but have barely engaged.

4. The source-tradition by problem matrix is mostly diagonal, and its off-diagonal gaps are founder opportunities. (Counts come from keyword matching on field lens, so they are approximate.)
- Faith and contemplative entries: about 39 in meaning, 15 in target and 11 in people, but 0 in safety, 0 in power and about 1 each in democracy and epistemics. Traditions speak to their congregations about dignity. Few feed model specifications (exceptions: CEFEAI, the AI Christian Benchmark, Gloo FAI, 84000, Khyentse, the Buddhism & AI Initiative). None addresses power concentration, though Catholic social teaching and Islamic economics have deep doctrine on concentrated wealth.
- Safety professions: 26 in safety and 10 in cooperation (nuclear), but 0 in minds. Patient-safety and incident-reporting practice (IHI, ECRI) has not been applied to companion-chatbot harms, and no one runs an epidemiology of AI harms.
- Clinical and developmental knowledge: 21 in minds and about 2 in target, so there is no 'developmental alignment' programme.
- Indigenous, Global South and feminist knowledge: 20 in justice, 2 in target and 0 in safety, agency or power. The Global South appears as rights-holders, not as a source of alignment targets or safety science.
- Labour: 16 in power and 6 in people, but nobody casts organising as a defence against gradual disempowerment.

5. The cooperation sector hides a split. About 15 entries work on multi-agent AI (CAIF, FOCAL, CLR, the Witt Lab, Concordia, the Anh Han group) and about 35 on peace and security. No mediation or peacebuilding entry works on AI–AI conflict, CLR is nearly alone on bargaining failure between AI systems, and nobody applies conflict transformation to the race between labs, or between the safety and ethics camps.

6. The same problem is held by communities that don't talk. Power concentration is worked on by the x-risk core (Formation, Longview, ACS, Forethought) and, separately, by antitrust, labour and public-AI organisations (AI Now, Open Markets, MIT Stone, unions, Humanity AI's $500M). The power sector holds 6 funders, mostly from the public-interest pool. In minds, UK AISI's 'socioaffective alignment' work sits apart from 27 adjacent clinical and child-safety organisations.

7. Funding is uneven by problem. Meaning has no dedicated funder at all; its work runs on religious institutions' own budgets and small FLI grants. Templeton's $60M+ for intelligence research sits in agency, framed as 'what intelligence is', not as safety or meaning. Target and AI minds each have one funder (Khyentse; the Digital Sentience Consortium).

8. Support for the people doing the work is thin. Of the 30 entries in that sector, only about 8 support AI-safety workers directly, and AI Safety Support has closed. Organisations with proven methods sit in the potential ring with no AI-safety programme: Garrison's Contemplative-Based Resilience, the Wellbeing Project, the Climate Psychology Alliance. The data-labelling and rating workforce (Data Workers' Inquiry, Data Labelers Association, Fairwork, Alphabet Workers Union) does part of the safety work, yet the field does not count it as its own.

9. Geography skews. Justice is the only sector where entries based outside the US, UK and Europe lead (about 20 of 51). Safety (22 of 48 in the US), minds (29 of 44 in the US or UK) and AI minds (24 of 33 in the US or UK) are Anglophone.

designs.reveals:
1) A coverage gradient by quadrant. Share on the aisafety.com classic map: It 21/95 (22%), Its 18/180 (10%), We 15/165 (9%), I 6/112 (5%). Share in the core ring: It 33%, We 15%, Its 13%, I 13%. Formal sciences are the classic map's home discipline: 17 of 25 are core and 13 of 25 are on the map. The quarters for minds and meaning are where the field is least visible to itself. Insiders looking for blind spots get this as one picture.

2) Near-empty core cells, which the mandala shows as blank wedges at the centre. Each has exactly one core entry: contemplative (Groundless Alignment), religion (FLI, there only through its religious-grants line) and arts (Geodesic Research). Rights has two (the AI Whistleblower Initiative and ILINA). The AI-safety core has almost no organisations rooted in contemplative, religious, artistic or rights traditions. These traditions engage from the bridge and adjacent rings.

3) Two different kinds of gap, which call for different funder strategies. (a) Parallel worlds: rights (39/55 adjacent), economy (24/40), religion (26/45) and psych (22/43) already work on AI at scale without an x-risk frame. Their potential rings are almost empty (rights 2, economy 2), so the opening is translation and convening, not recruitment. (b) Untapped reservoirs: life sciences (11/28 potential), contemplative (13/41) and systems (13/43) hold relevant knowledge with only light AI engagement, e.g. CASCB, ISAL, the St Andrews diverse-intelligences centre, the Bateson Institute, the Cybernetics Society, the System Dynamics Society, Inner Development Goals, the Presencing Institute and Esalen. That is where new founders and fellowships could pull people in.

4) AI minds is an inward-built field: 22 of its 28 entries are core or bridge, with only 4 adjacent and 2 potential. Yet per the scrape only 1 of the 28 (CaML) is on the classic map. It has barely connected to the older consciousness-science and contemplative establishments (Sussex, the Arizona Center for Consciousness Studies, QRI and Essentia are the exceptions). It is also a quarter-border neighbour of life sciences, which is where the angle notes' missing bridge sits: metacognition and introspection evals for safety, not only for welfare.

5) Scale, tested on a systematic 69-entry sample: society 29%, AI system 26%, civilisation and planet 19%, person 12%, community and institution 12%, AI ecosystems and the human-AI dyad about 1-2% each. Extrapolated, that is roughly 25 dyad-focused and roughly 12 AI-ecosystem entries in the full roster. These two middle levels are the least populated, yet they are where companion and delusion harms happen and where collusion and gradual disempowerment would emerge.

6) Inner and outer work: roughly 90% of entries are outer work only, about 30 do inner work on people, about 20 bring inner knowledge to outer targets, and about 6 deliberately integrate the two (int/a, MAPLE, Connecting Intelligence, Wisdom + AI, the Vervaeke Foundation). The integrated cell is int/a's natural white space.

7) Translation across quadrants: crossing the field quadrant with the problem quadrant shows that most widening carries I or We knowledge to We or Its problems (culture, governance). Very few entries carry it into It problems, i.e. technical alignment. The exceptions are contemplative alignment (FLIP, CSAS, MMI, Positive AI Labs), faith benchmarks (CEFEAI, Gloo, the AI Christian Benchmark) and narrative-as-prior work (Geodesic, Hyperstition). Founders should look at these off-diagonal cells.

8) Border neighbours as bridge prompts: minds|life (consciousness and neuroscience); safety|systems (STAMP/STPA for agent ecosystems, so far an isolated voice through Dobbe and Leveson); rights|collective (participatory audits); religion|contemplative (chaplains and spiritual-emergency networks for chatbot-induced spiritual delusion, which the angle notes found unaddressed).

9) Testing the integral frames themselves. The quadrants discriminate well as a layout: the quarters hold 95 to 180 entries and show the gradient above. As an entry-level facet they mostly duplicate the field facet, so the quadrant is derived from the field. Scale discriminates moderately and is legible. Inner/outer is heavily skewed, which makes it a poor filter but a revealing colour layer. The five principles cannot be coded reliably across 552 entries (speed of wisdom and fractal altruism especially), so they become sparse badges for the int/a-community persona only. Developmental levels (Kegan or ego stages), lines, states and types were dropped: they cannot be scored for organisations and would read as ranking them. A funder or an aisafety.com editor can read the plain quarter labels (minds, meaning, mechanisms, systems) without knowing Wilber.

10) Persona entry points: funders start from the potential and adjacent rings of the I and We quarters; founders from the off-diagonal cells in the field x problem matrix; outsiders find their own sector and its neighbours; insiders read the coverage gradient; int/a members filter by inner/outer and principle badges.
