Sector × ring counts (core/bridge/adjacent/potential), with the number already on the classic map in brackets:
- systems 19/8/2/10 [13]
- life 7/10/5/10 [5]
- minds 8/15/4/2 [1]
- psych 1/8/23/2 [1]
- inner 5/9/15/15 [3]
- faith 1/15/27/7 [2]
- philo 8/7/14/4 [4]
- plural 4/6/20/1 [2]
- futures 12/15/16/10 [9]
- civic 7/16/27/7 [4]
- lawsoc 3/8/20/2 [2]
- econ 8/8/21/1 [5]
- peace 7/19/10/4 [6]
- safety 4/15/12/8 [3]

(1) The classic map's interdisciplinarity is mostly maths and complexity. 13 of the 60 roster entries already on aisafety.com fall in systems, the only sector where core entries outnumber every other ring. The core is thinnest on the humanities-and-traditions half of the wheel: psych has 1 core entry out of 34, faith 1 out of 50, lawsoc 3, plural 4 and inner 5. On the mandala that half has an almost empty inner ring, which is the blind spot the brief described.

(2) Fields take two shapes.
- Built inside-out: the safety community made them, and their roots in the parent discipline are shallow. Minds has 23 of 29 entries in core or bridge; mainstream consciousness societies and funders (ASSC, Kavli, Simons, Allen) have no AI-safety window. Systems has 19 core entries, while SFI and CSH Vienna have no gradual-disempowerment programme.
- Built outside-in: large and self-organised, but cut off from the core. Psych has 23 adjacent entries, faith 27, plural 20, lawsoc 20, and econ 21 (mostly unions and labour economics).
- The bridge ring is thickest in peace (19) and safety (15). Older risk disciplines (arms control, safety-case engineering, aviation certification) have already crossed over, which offers a template for the other fields.

(3) int/a's own milieu is potential more than practice. Inner has the most potential-ring entries (15 of 44) and no funder at all. Its engagement is mostly events and content: Esalen, IEC, Tricycle, SAND. Empty cells a founder could fill:
- wisdom and metacognition evaluations;
- chaplaincy for spiritual delusions induced by AI (Chaplaincy Innovation Lab is only potential);
- resilience for the field on the Garrison CBR model.

(4) Funding geometry. Of 33 funders, 9 sit in civic: Humanity AI, EAISF, Mozilla, Omidyar, Current AI, Coefficient, EIP, FLF, SHIFT. That is the 'ethics and accountability' money, which the angle notes say almost never co-funds with x-risk money. Psych, plural and minds each have exactly one funder: Young Futures (about $1.4M), IDRC AI4D, and the Digital Sentience Consortium. Big pools with no safety framing (JTF's $60M+, TWCF's Diverse Intelligences, Lloyd's Register Foundation) sit in faith, life and safety. They are natural co-funding partners for new funders.

(5) Thin potential rings (econ 1, plural 1, psych 2, minds 2, lawsoc 2) mark neighbours nobody has tried to recruit. Examples: no developmental cohort study with an AI module, no consciousness society engaged, and almost no Global South political-economy groups beyond Aapti and RIA. Some of these gaps are artefacts of the search, which ran only in English and with exhausted WebSearch budgets. The map should label them as such.

(6) Gaps in the field × problem matrix that this scheme makes visible:
- faith × values evaluations: only Gloo, CEFEAI and the AI Christian Benchmark feed technical artefacts;
- life × welfare and foundations: comparative-cognition evaluations for agency and sentience;
- systems × power;
- civic × assurance: nobody red-teams AI facilitators;
- psych × values: developmental psychology as alignment theory;
- minds × psych: welfare researchers and psychiatrists study how people attribute minds to AI from opposite sides;
- econ × field-building: there has been no standing pipeline into TAI economics since GPI closed;
- systems (cybernetics societies) × foundations.

(7) Geography, by stated location: about 175 entries in North America, 134 in the UK and Ireland, 111 in continental Europe, 44 in Asia-Pacific, 17 in Sub-Saharan Africa, 9 in Latin America, 7 in the Middle East and North Africa, and 55 global or distributed. For int/a's hubs:
- London: 44 entries.
- Berlin: 14 (Weizenbaum, HIIG, AlgorithmWatch, MPIB CHM, KIRA, SUPERRR, MAI).
- Paris: 14 (Café IA, Make.org, SaferAI, IRI Pompidou, everyone.AI, Current AI, OECD and UNESCO units).
- There is no independent research on companion-AI harms in China, Japan or Korea.

(8) Status: 18 entries are unclear and 1 is closed. Dormant niches (the Consilience Project, Equilibria Network, CTNS Virtuous AI, AI Safety Support) are open ground the founder view highlights.

scores.comments: This is the strongest base scheme. The sectors name disciplines that an outsider recognises. The wheel puts related traditions next to each other, so a seam between sectors is where a bridge would form. The boundary rules are the most thorough of the four, and it is the only scheme where Indigenous & decolonial has its own sector. That sector's empty core and bridge rings are the clearest single gap on any of the four maps. I checked its assignments against the other two field-based schemes, matching categories where the three line up. Two schemes agree 86% (integral) and 83% (navigator), the highest of any pair, and all three agree on 76% of entries. Religion, peace and safety are very stable (Jaccard overlap 0.9 or more). Psychology, contemplative and law are weaker (0.57 to 0.86). Spot-check problems: (1) 'Mind & brain' puts NeuroAI (AE Studio, Astera, Eon, WBAI) together with the AI-welfare field (Eleos, Rethink Priorities, PRISM, Anthropic Model Welfare). That buries the field the classic map most obviously misses: about 29 entries, 23 of them core or bridge, almost none on aisafety.com. (2) The Buddhist boundary is inconsistent. Buddhism & AI Initiative goes to religion, while CSAS, Arising and MMI go to contemplative; the navigator puts all four in faith. (3) Generalist funders are arbitrary. Schmidt Sciences is in arts here, philosophy in integral and lawsoc in navigator. CIFAR is law, safety or lawsoc. FLI and Coefficient read oddly to a funder. (4) Wisdom & Culture Lab and the Center for Practical Wisdom go to psychology, but to contemplative or inner in the other two schemes. Children's rights go to law here and to psych in the navigator. The proposed public facet set is too heavy: seven facets, and only the primary one is assigned. The transfer facet is the best secondary idea in all four submissions. Way of knowing would be hard to code consistently and could stay as an internal int/a lens.

The problem names read well for funders and AI-safety insiders. The extra facets (lever, locus, risk framing) are excellent. As the primary facet, though, it has three structural problems. (1) It partly encodes proximity. The boundary between 'target' and 'meaning' is model-facing versus community-facing, which is close to a ring split: target's ring profile is 5 core / 17 bridge / 7 adjacent / 2 potential, meaning's is 0 / 7 / 35 / 8. So 'meaning has 0 core entries', the scheme's headline finding, follows from the definition. The empty cells stop meaning what the mandala needs them to mean. (2) Many sectors are fields under another name. I cross-tabbed it against the disciplines scheme. Futures is 87% arts, power 82% economics, democracy 81% democracy, safety 77% safety and cooperation 69% peace. Normalised mutual information with the field schemes is 0.57 to 0.62. Only target (23% from its largest discipline), agency (32%) and people (37%) truly cut across fields. A single-label field x problem matrix would therefore be mostly diagonal. (3) The calls are fragile. KIRA goes to justice. Forethought and the Hong Kong Catastrophic Risk Centre go to metacrisis, which stretches 'metacrisis' to cover long-term trajectory in general. FLI, Coefficient, Schmidt, CIFAR and BRAID go to people. TruthfulAI goes to epistemics. WCC's red lines go to justice while AIFCS goes to meaning. Cooperation (54) is 37 peace entries plus a multi-agent AI cluster that it hides. A researcher from another field cannot find where they belong, and AI safety already uses these problem names (alignment target, cooperative AI, power concentration, epistemics). So as the primary facet it drifts back toward the classic map's own agenda. Used instead as multi-valued matrix columns, it is very valuable.

The sector labels are plain language, and using the four quadrants as the four quarters of the mandala, rather than as labels, is elegant. It produces the clearest single picture in all four schemes: share on the classic map by quarter runs from 22% (mechanisms and machines) to 5% (minds and experience). Dropping developmental stages, which could not be scored and would read as a ranking, was the right call, as was the warning that rings must not imply height. Making Consciousness & AI Minds its own sector is correct: 28 entries, 22 core or bridge, 1 on the classic map. Its field assignments agree 86% with the disciplines scheme. Weaknesses: (1) There is no Indigenous sector. GIDA, Te Hiku, Te Mana Raraunga and Local Contexts go to rights, and GTDF and Dreaming Beyond AI go to arts. The strongest gap signal, an empty Indigenous core and bridge, disappears, and Indigenous knowledge is read as a rights claim. (2) Putting futures with complexity in 'Systems, Complexity & Futures' leaves the Millennium Project, IFTF, Long Now, OECD foresight and AI Futures Project next to Santa Fe, and arts shrinks to 22 entries (4%). Collective is 60 (10.9%), just over the cap. (3) Each field gets one quadrant, which misreads some entries (CHT's analysis of race dynamics sits in the 'I' quarter). Scale was estimated from a 69-entry sample, inner/outer counts are approximate, and the principle badges are subjective. Keep the badges and the inner/outer layer for the int/a persona only.

It has the best practical layer of the four. The engagement facet (staff roles, fellowships, open funding calls, events, courses, communities, open contribution, 'door to open') answers 'how do I get involved', and status, maturity, geography, int/a hubs, the classic-map overlay and concrete persona entry views are ready to build. It has the most even sectors (evenness 0.992). Its observation that some fields were built from the AI-safety side outward and others grew outside and stay cut off is a useful funder framing, and it honestly flags thin potential rings that may be search artefacts. Robustness is the weak point. It agrees least with the other field schemes (82 to 83%), and the spot-checks show why. (1) 'Global Majority & Indigenous' is a standpoint, and the scheme breaks its own rule (a discipline beats the standpoint): CISAI (a cooperative-AI fellowship), ORCG (catastrophic-risk studies), the African Hub on AI Safety, Peace and Security, ILINA, Beijing-AISI, IDRC and LIRNEasia are filed by standpoint, while ACCORD and Concordia AI go by discipline. (2) 'Inner' takes in CFAR, ESPR, Rethink Wellbeing, Mental Health Navigator, AI Safety Support and the Climate Psychology Alliance. Calling applied rationality and therapy referral 'contemplative & inner development' will confuse outsiders and blurs the contemplative gap. (3) 'Futures' puts Metaculus, FRI, Sage, Sentinel and Mantic together with Superflux, CSI and Better Images of AI, so its ring profile averages two different communities. (4) Children's rights go to psych, and cooperative AI (CAIF, FOCAL, CLR) goes to econ. The practical facets need data the roster lacks and go out of date quickly, so someone has to own them.

best_ideas_to_graft: From the disciplines scheme: order the 14 sectors as a wheel of intellectual kinship, so that seams are where bridges form, and draw two-tradition bridges on the seam using a secondary-traditions facet.

From the disciplines scheme: keep Indigenous & decolonial knowledge as its own sector, defined by knowledge tradition, not geography. Its empty core and bridge rings (16 entries, all adjacent or potential) are the clearest gap on any of the four maps. Show Majority-World location with a separate geography facet.

From the disciplines scheme: add a direction-of-transfer facet (into the model / into institutions / protecting its own constituency / convening its community / latent knowledge). It tells a funder whether a tradition has reached the model or only talks to its own people.

From the disciplines scheme: show disciplines that have no sector at all (anthropology, history, linguistics, education, library science, accounting and audit, operations research, epidemiology of AI harms, Hindu, Sikh, Shinto and Bahá'í institutions) as an explicit legend of absent fields. These are openings for founders.

From the disciplines scheme: a span facet (single tradition / two-tradition bridge / integrative hub / generalist funder), so hubs and funders are visibly provisional instead of silently mis-sectored.

From the problem scheme: a problem facet coded with 1 to 3 values per entry, used as the columns of the field x problem matrix. Split cooperation into 'multi-agent AI' and 'war, weapons and international coordination', as the navigator did, so the multi-agent cluster stays visible. Keep 'people doing the work' and 'what AI should value' as distinct columns.

From the problem scheme: a risk-framing facet (catastrophic / structural and gradual / present harms / flourishing / critical or deflationary). It makes the gap between the safety and ethics camps visible and lets funders match their mandate.

From the problem scheme: the theory-of-change lever facet (understand, measure, build, set norms, law, convene, widen participation, organise, form people, imagine, fund), plus a view that pairs communities working the same problem without talking to each other (power concentration: Formation and Longview versus Open Markets, AI Now and the unions; minds: UK AISI's socioaffective work versus the clinicians).

From the integral scheme: split Consciousness & AI Minds out of the brain and life sciences. The AI-welfare and relational AI-minds field (about 29 entries, mostly core or bridge, almost none on aisafety.com) is a major blind spot and needs its own wedge.

From the integral scheme: four plain-language arcs as the macro-grouping, which also serve as the phone-width fallback, and a stated design rule that rings measure proximity, not developmental height.

From the integral scheme: tag the two thin middle levels, the human-AI relationship and ecosystems of AI agents, as a locus tag, and frame funder strategy as 'parallel worlds' (translate and convene) versus 'untapped reservoirs' (recruit and fund fellowships).
From the integral scheme: an inner/outer colour layer and sparse principle badges, shown only in the int/a-community view.

judgements.recommendation:
Radial sectors should be the home field or tradition, not the problem. My reasons:
(a) The brief is to map adjacent fields, and the outside persona asks 'where does my field fit?'
(b) Field is independent of proximity, so an empty sector x ring cell means something. The problem scheme's target/meaning boundary encodes how far an entry engages the model, so its hollow cores are partly built in.
(c) It is more robust. Three independent field schemes agree 82 to 86% pairwise and 76% three-way at a coarse level, with religion, peace and safety at Jaccard overlap 0.9 or more. The problem designer estimates 15 to 20% of single-label problem calls are judgement calls, and my spot-checks found several weak ones (KIRA to justice, Forethought to metacrisis, FLI, Coefficient, Schmidt and CIFAR to people).
(d) Fields do not re-describe the classic map. Several problem sectors are AI safety's own agenda terms.

Base the wheel on the disciplines scheme's 14 sectors and kinship order, with these edits:
- Split Consciousness & AI Minds into its own sector, as integral and navigator do.
- To stay at 14, merge formal sciences with complexity, cybernetics and metacrisis systems into 'Formal & complexity sciences', and move NeuroAI and cognitive science in with biology as 'Life & brain sciences'.
- Keep Indigenous & decolonial as a knowledge tradition. File Global South policy organisations by discipline and show region through a geography facet.
- Put field-health services in psychology, forecasting and collective epistemics in democracy & collective intelligence, and futures studies with arts & narrative.
Re-sorting the existing assignments into this cut gives 16 to 54 entries per sector (2.9 to 9.8%). The ring profiles stay telling: Indigenous has 0 core and 0 bridge, AI minds 8/15/4/2, contemplative 1/10/13/13, formal & complexity 23/10/5/10. Group the sectors into four plain arcs (sciences, inner life, humanities & cultures, society & institutions); the arcs are also the phone-width view.

Rings are proximity (core, bridge, adjacent, potential). Show classic-map status as a filled versus hollow dot, and never imply that the core is 'higher'.

Colour is the problem arc of the entry's main problem (the AI itself / human minds & meaning / living & deciding together / conflict, risk & civilisation). Four colours are readable, and a sector's colour mix shows at a glance whether a tradition reaches the machine or only the human side. Let users switch the colour layer to direction of transfer, risk framing, or inner/outer (the last only in the int/a view). Draw generalist funders as a separate band or glyph with links to the sectors they fund; do not place them in a sector.

The matrix has 14 home-field rows and about 15 problem columns, coded 1 to 3 per entry. Shade each cell by ring mix and label empty cells as openings for founders, noting where a cell may be empty only because of search effort. Add a tradition x tradition bridge matrix built from the secondary-traditions facet. The filters are problem, risk framing, lever and transfer, span or funder, engagement, geography, int/a hub, status, maturity and classic-map status.

The problem facet must be multi-valued. Single-label problem and field are strongly correlated (normalised mutual information 0.57 to 0.62; futures is 87% arts, power 82% economics, democracy 81% democracy), so a single-label matrix would be mostly a diagonal.

Before publishing, double-code about 100 entries (Buddhist organisations, hubs, generalist funders, Global South policy organisations, and the psychology/contemplative and law/indigenous boundaries) and report kappa. All four designers worked from the same 'field lens' column, which inflates the agreement figures above. My cross-scheme join and agreement scripts are in <scratchpad>/judge/ (joined.json, agree.py, xtab.py, disagree.tsv).

scores.comments: The strongest base for the radial sectors. Ordering the wheel by intellectual kinship makes adjacency mean something: bridges sit on the seams, and bridges that cross the wheel stand out as new territory. It keeps Formal sciences (16 core, 0 adjacent) apart from Living & complex systems (10 core, 15 potential). That split shows a maths core the classic map has fully absorbed next to a cybernetics and systems tradition it has never met. The Navigator merger hides both. Care for AI-safety workers goes into psychology (psych_fieldhealth), not contemplative, so int/a's own sector honestly shows 1 core entry (Groundless Alignment). The way-of-knowing facet is the best operationalisation of full-spectrum knowing in any of the four schemes. The direction-of-transfer facet (into the model, into institutions, protecting its domain, convening) captures the key int/a finding: the inner traditions convene their own communities but rarely put their methods into models. The list of disciplines with no sector at all is a ready-made gap register for founders. Spot-checks against the roster: FLI goes to religion and Schmidt Sciences to arts, both arbitrary, as the designer admits. Geodesic goes to arts, which breaks the scheme's own 'method, not topic' rule, since Geodesic's method is ML pretraining. Cyborgism goes to arts: defensible by method, but people looking for AI-minds work won't find it there. SUPERRR, Tattle and IT for Change sit in a sector labelled 'Indigenous & decolonial', which feminist and Indian civic-tech groups may not recognise as their home. Toda and the Peacemakers Network going to peace follows the stated rule, which is good. The UI gaps are real: there is no problem facet, so the scheme can't build the field x problem matrix it relies on itself, and it has no practical or persona facets. Only the primary facet is coded.

The only scheme that is truly a different axis. It overlaps the Traditions Wheel by about 61%, while the three field schemes overlap each other by 78-84%. That makes it the natural second dimension, not a rival primary. It produces the most actionable findings for the brief's 'list of problems for founders': meaning has 0 core entries out of 50, and minds has 1 out of 44. AI moral status is an off-map field, and inside it the EA welfare wing and the relational wing barely meet. The source x problem diagonal yields concrete openings: patient-safety practice applied to companion harms, developmental alignment, and Catholic social teaching applied to power concentration. Counting the data-labelling workforce as part of the safety workforce ('people doing the work') is an original move. The lever, locus and framing facets are good; the 'critical/deflationary' framing lets DAIR, Critical AI and Bioneers sit on the map without being forced into a harm frame. As the primary radial facet it works against the brief: researchers from other fields can't find themselves, and the unit the brief named is the adjacent field. Robustness is the weakest of the four, because sectors are statements of intent and the designer admits 15-20% judgement calls. Spot-checks: Forethought and the Hong Kong Catastrophic Risk Centre are in metacrisis, next to Game B and the Club of Rome, a stretch. Ostrom goes to democracy and JTF to agency, both speculative. FLI, Coefficient, Schmidt and CIFAR all land in 'people doing the work', so funders share a sector with therapist directories. WCC goes to justice while AIFCS goes to meaning. Meaning is 32/50 religious bodies, so it works as a polite synonym for religion and risks framing faith as talking to congregations rather than as a knowledge source. Old Ways, New in target is a good call.

It uses int/a's own lens with discernment. The integral frames that can't be coded for organisations (stages, lines, states, types) are dropped because they would read as a ranking. The designer warns that the rings measure proximity, not developmental height, which the map's visual design must respect. The quadrant gradient is the single best one-picture headline: classic-map coverage is 22% in It, 10% in Its, 9% in We and 5% in I. The level-of-the-whole facet surfaces a real blind spot: the human-AI dyad and AI-ecosystem levels are thin, and those are where companion harms and collusion arise. The inner/outer colour layer finds the 'integrated' cell (int/a, MAPLE, Connecting Intelligence, Wisdom + AI, Vervaeke), which is int/a's white space. Grouping problems by quadrant gives the matrix a natural structure. Weaknesses: the field facet is about 84% the same as the Traditions Wheel, but with worse cuts. Futures studies (Millennium Project, IFTF, CIFS, UNESCO FL) goes into systems, which shrinks arts to 22. Indigenous organisations (Te Hiku, GIDA, Local Contexts, Masakhane) go into rights, so Indigenous knowledge reads only as a rights claim. That is a real fidelity cost for a 'widening' map. Other spot-checks: CaML and Cyborgism go to minds, Witt Lab to formal, CIFAR to safety and Hybrid Intelligence to collective. I/We/It/Its is opaque outside int/a, and deriving the quadrant from the field mislabels organisations whose focus differs from their field (CHT). Scale was coded on only 69 entries.

The best product thinking of the four. It has persona entry points with concrete default views and an engagement facet (jobs, fellowships, grants, events, courses, communities, contribute, and 'door to open' for potential partners). Maturity, geography, int/a hubs (London, Berlin, Paris, online), status (dormant niches as founder signals), the classic-map overlay and a coded problem facet all map directly onto the five personas. Its sector cuts weaken the gap picture, though. 'Complexity, systems & maths' puts Iliad, MAISI, ARIA, Simplex and Resolution with the Club of Rome, Bateson and Game B: 19 core entries, almost all formal, averaged with the empty cybernetics core. Its 5 'inner' core entries are all EA field-health and rationality services (Rethink Wellbeing, Upgradable, AISS, CFAR, ESPR), with no contemplative organisation among them. That fills int/a's own core cell artificially and blurs the finding the brief most needs. 'Futures, narrative & arts' (53) puts Metaculus, FRI, Sentinel, QURI, Full Fact and C2PA together with art and journalism. Cooperative AI (CAIF, FOCAL, CLR, Modeling Cooperation) sits in econ next to unions. The 'Global Majority & Indigenous' sector makes Majority-World work visible, a real plus given the Anglophone skew. But it puts a standpoint or geography on the primary facet, absorbing core x-risk organisations (ILINA, ORCG, Beijing-AISI, CISAI) by location and culture, and the rule that standpoint wins only when it is the contribution leaves taggers too much judgement. Children's rights placed with child development in psych is a defensible, useful choice.

judgements.recommendation:
Radial sectors: the home tradition, built on the disciplines designer's 14-sector Traditions Wheel and its kinship order. Three independently designed field schemes agree on 78-84% of placements, which is strong evidence that tradition is a robust, recognisable primary facet. It also answers the brief's unit (adjacent fields) and the first question an outsider asks ('I'm a psychoanalyst / cyberneticist / theologian: where am I?'). Of the three field cuts, this one reveals the most. It keeps Formal sciences apart from Living & complex systems, gives Indigenous & decolonial knowledge its own sector (empty core and bridge cells are the finding), and keeps field-health services out of the contemplative sector. Four fixes before use. (1) Rename the Indigenous sector to cover the feminist and Black traditions its definition already includes, or move SUPERRR, Tattle and IT for Change to Law/STS. (2) Take generalist funders out of the sector counts and draw them as a funding overlay. (3) Apply the 'method, not topic' rule consistently: Geodesic is not arts. (4) Keep the families (Sciences & engineering; Human & inner life; Humanities & cultures; Society & institutions) as the phone-width fallback and as plain-language quarters in place of I/We/It/Its.

Rings: the four proximity rings (core, bridge, adjacent, potential), with the classic-map overlay as a dot outline. Follow the integral designer's rule: the centre must not read as higher or better, and the potential ring gets full visual weight, because that is where widening happens.

Colour, default: the problem arc of each entry's primary problem, in 4 hues (the AI itself / human minds & meaning / living & deciding together / conflict, risk & civilisation). Problem overlaps tradition by only about 60%, so colour adds real information instead of repeating the sector. The int/a finding then shows at a glance: religion, contemplative and psychology wedges glow 'human minds & meaning' and almost never 'the AI itself'. Colour also connects the mandala to the matrix and to how funders think. Switchable colour layers: direction of transfer (the sharpest int/a lens), way of knowing, inner/outer work, and level of the whole.

Matrix axes: rows are the 14 home traditions in wheel order, grouped by family; columns are the problems designer's 14 problems, grouped by its 4 arcs. Problem is many-valued, with a primary problem. Cells show counts with ring shading (core/bridge share), and a toggle adds secondary-tradition memberships so bridges appear. Add a tradition x tradition bridge matrix from the secondary-traditions facet as a second view; bridges across the wheel mark new ground.

Filters: ring, classic map, span (including generalist funder), sub-tradition, way of knowing, transfer direction, lever, locus, risk framing, level of the whole, inner/outer, region plus Majority-World flag, int/a hub, engagement, maturity, status, organisation kind. Persona entry points follow the navigator's specification.

Before publishing, run the full coding pass for every secondary facet with two independent coders on a stratified sample of about 60 entries, and report agreement. Problem focus and transfer direction are the least robust facets, so show each entry's second-best placement. Label empty cells that are search artefacts (statistics/OR, non-English sources) differently from genuine absences.
